newsitem.title: USA: Sportscaster to plead not guilty to sex charges.
newsitem.headline: Sportscaster to plead not guilty to sex charges.

text.p: Veteran sportscaster Marv Albert plans to plead innocent to charges that he bit and sexually assaulted a woman in a hotel room in February, his lawyer told an Arlington court Tuesday.

At an arraignment, Judge Benjamin Kendrick set Sept. 22 for a jury trial in Arlington County Circuit Court. Albert, 53, sat silently during the six-minute hearing flanked by his lawyer Gerard Treanor and a woman identified as his fiancee.

Treanor said Albert planned to plead not guilty to the two counts handed up a grand jury last week. He was accused of forcing a 42-year-old woman to perform oral sex and biting her repeatedly on the back.
He was formally charged with one felony count of forcible sodomy, which in Virginia includes oral sex, and one misdemeanor count of assault and battery.

"We intend to enter pleas of not guilty to both counts," Treanor told the court. He said "a number of analyses" were being carried out on Albert's behalf. The lawyer did not immediately return a phone call seeking further details.

Richard Trodden, the Commonwealth's Attorney for Arlington County, said he had no objection to letting Albert remain free until trial but he required the sportscaster to sign a statement promising to pay $1,000 if he failed to appear.

After the hearing, Albert was taken to the Arlington County detention centre where he was to be photographed and fingerprinted, police said. Under Virginia law, he has until the trial date to enter his formal plea.

The court heard no references to Albert's accuser. One day after his indictment became public it was learned she faces criminal charges in the District of Columbia for allegedly threatening to kill an ex-boyfriend, who is a district police officer, his girlfriend and his dog.
The woman told police that Albert, a friend for about 10 years, invited her to join him in his Arlington hotel room after a New York Knicks-Washington Bullets basketball game.
Despite the indictment, Albert called the play-by-play of NBA playoff games between the Chicago Bulls and Miami Heat in Florida on Saturday and Monday and is scheduled call the NBA Finals next month.

"I would like to reaffirm my innocence," he said in a prepared statement at a news conference in New York last Thursday. He criticised police and prosecutors for not interviewing him about the charges before the indictment was made public a week ago.

Albert just completed his 30th season as the voice of the Knicks and his 32nd season broadcasting for the New York Rangers. He also calls NFL games on NBC and has worked numerous other events for the network including boxing and the Summer Olympics.
The forcible sodomy charge carries a maximum penalty of five years to life in prison and the assault and battery is punishable by up to 12 months in prison and/or a $2,500 fine.
